{
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "confidence": 0.6,
  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R55"],
      "pins": ["R55.1", "R55.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R55 is labelled with value \"24k\" in the schematic and SPICE deck (R55 VOUTN VOUTP 24k), but its library description and MPN say the part is 24 ohms: the MPN FRC0805J240TSD uses the 240 code, which denotes 24Ω.",
      "expected": "A value field that matches the part actually fitted. If the part is 24Ω, the value should read 24R; a 24k value would be roughly 1000x too high for this node.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R55\") (value \"24k\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(field (name \"MPN\") \"FRC0805J240TSD\")"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R55 VOUTN VOUTP 24k"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the 24Ω part is fitted, the value mismatch means the design or BOM disagrees with the intended resistance. If 24k is really intended, the MPN is wrong. Either way, the VOUTN–VOUTP network does not match its documented part.",
      "confidence": 0.6
    },
    {
      "category": "open_connection",
      "components": ["D26", "D40", "D47", "R37", "R32", "R53"],
      "pins": ["D26.2", "D40.2", "D47.2"],
      "nets": ["/NET0003"],
      "observed": "The anodes of the three status LEDs D26, D40 and D47 are all on net /NET0003, and that net has no other connection. None of the anodes reaches +3V3 or any other supply. Their cathodes drive through R37, R32 and R53 from the Ethernet/PI LED outputs.",
      "expected": "These LEDs are configured as cathode-driven indicators: the anode should be tied to +3V3 and the cathode pulled through a resistor to the active-low LED output. An isolated anode net means the LEDs cannot be powered.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"5\") (name \"/NET0003\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"D26\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D40\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D47\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"D47\") (pin \"1\") (pinfunction \"K\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"R53\") (pin \"1\") (pintype \"passive\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "Ethernet and PI activity indicators D26, D40 and D47 never light, so the link and activity status is not shown to the user.",
      "confidence": 0.5
    },
    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["R80", "D9"],
      "pins": ["R80.2", "D9.2", "D9.4"],
      "nets": ["NET0138", "Net-(D9-K2)"],
      "observed": "R80 is connected between the cathode K2 of D9 (Net-(D9-K2)) and net NET0138. NET0138 is also the anode A2 of D9 and the output of U48. The LED is therefore bypassed by its own series resistor, and the resistor's other end is not returned to ground. The first half of the same LED package, K1, uses R84 to GND.",
      "expected": "By analogy with the K1 half (R84 pin 2 to GND), R80's far end should return to GND so that LED2 is driven as a current-limited indicator between its anode and ground.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R80\") (value \"130R\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"106\") (name \"NET0138\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"D9\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"A2\") (pintype \"input\")) (node (ref \"J34\") (pin \"6\") ...) (node (ref \"R80\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"U48\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"Y\") (pintype \"output\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"155\") (name \"Net-(D9-K1)\") ... (node (ref \"R84\") (pin \"1\") ...)"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R80 Net-_D9-K2_ NET0138 130"}
      ],
      "impact": "LED2 of D9 is effectively shorted by R80, so the e-stop/sink status indicator never lights. The fault is cosmetic, but it indicates a wiring error in the e-stop indicator path.",
      "confidence": 0.35
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The clearest deviation is R55, whose value of 24k contradicts its 24Ω description and MPN. Two further candidates are the status-LED anode net /NET0003, which is isolated from any supply, and R80, which bypasses D9's LED2 instead of returning it to ground. The spec does not cover these parts, so the verdict relies on netlist consistency."
}

anomalies.observed: R55 is labelled with value "24k" in the schematic and SPICE deck (R55 VOUTN VOUTP 24k), but its library description and MPN say the part is 24 ohms: the MPN FRC0805J240TSD uses the 240 code, which denotes 24Ω.
anomalies.expected: A value field that matches the part actually fitted. If the part is 24Ω, the value should read 24R; a 24k value would be roughly 1000x too high for this node.

evidence.quote: 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS

anomalies.impact: If the 24Ω part is fitted, the value mismatch means the design or BOM disagrees with the intended resistance. If 24k is really intended, the MPN is wrong. Either way, the VOUTN–VOUTP network does not match its documented part.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of the three status LEDs D26, D40 and D47 are all on net /NET0003, and that net has no other connection. None of the anodes reaches +3V3 or any other supply. Their cathodes drive through R37, R32 and R53 from the Ethernet/PI LED outputs.
anomalies.expected: These LEDs are configured as cathode-driven indicators: the anode should be tied to +3V3 and the cathode pulled through a resistor to the active-low LED output. An isolated anode net means the LEDs cannot be powered.
anomalies.impact: Ethernet and PI activity indicators D26, D40 and D47 never light, so the link and activity status is not shown to the user.

anomalies.observed: R80 is connected between the cathode K2 of D9 (Net-(D9-K2)) and net NET0138. NET0138 is also the anode A2 of D9 and the output of U48. The LED is therefore bypassed by its own series resistor, and the resistor's other end is not returned to ground. The first half of the same LED package, K1, uses R84 to GND.
anomalies.expected: By analogy with the K1 half (R84 pin 2 to GND), R80's far end should return to GND so that LED2 is driven as a current-limited indicator between its anode and ground.
anomalies.impact: LED2 of D9 is effectively shorted by R80, so the e-stop/sink status indicator never lights. The fault is cosmetic, but it indicates a wiring error in the e-stop indicator path.
